title: Auto Loans: Autopay from PCB Checking
content:
Autopay on an Auto Loans account draws each monthly installment automatically from a Piedmont Crescent Bank checking account. This policy states who may set it up or end it, which account may pay, and how the arrangement behaves.

## Rule

- **What autopay does.** On each due date the monthly payment is debited from the borrower's PCB checking account.
- **Paying account.** At enrollment the paying account must be a checking account belonging to the same customer and in active status, as the checking records show.
- **Whose decision.** Starting or ending autopay is an instruction the borrower gives about their own money, and it can be given only for a loan in active or delinquent status.
- **Installment unchanged.** A change in APR leaves the monthly payment where it is; it alters how each payment divides between interest and principal, and so the size of the final installment.
- **Returned autopay debits.** An autopay debit that comes back unpaid is treated under the returned payment rules, while the loan's enrollment stays in place.

## Clauses withdrawn from this policy

Two passages of the earlier wording of this policy are **no longer in force**:

- the clause under which enrolling brought the autopay discount into the APR, within the combined limit and the floor, starting with the next installment falling due at least 5 calendar days after enrollment; and
- the clause under which cancelling took the discount out on that same timetable, for products set to withdraw the autopay discount when autopay ends.

The rate written when autopay is started or ended now follows the Auto Loans rules that took their place. The 5-day lead period belonged only to those retired clauses.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical situations)

**The borrower names a checking account that belongs to someone else.** It cannot be the paying account; the account must be the borrower's own.

**The named account is closed.** It cannot be enrolled as the paying account, because only an active account qualifies at enrollment.

**An autopay debit bounces.** The returned payment rules apply to it, and the enrollment is not ended.

superseded_clauses: cancelling removes it on the same schedule when autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true
Enrolling adds the autopay discount to the APR, within the cap and floor of auto_agg_relationship_discount, from the next installment due at least autopay_lead_days calendar days after enrollment
